Superintendent Dr. Peter Lancia discussed the memo in the packet regarding the special services department 
leadership restructuring in which he explained that the Director of Special Services, Kelli Fogg, retired last year and 
the school department was unable to find a successful replacement.  Ms. Fogg agreed to serve as Director of Special 
Services as a contracted services employee which does not provide benefits. 
 
Superintendent Dr. Peter Lancia explained that they continued to advertise for a Director of Special Services but has 
been unsuccessful.  Ms. Fogg has agreed to continue in the position as contracted services along with two assistant 
directors; one at 100% funding from the general fund the second at 20% funding from the general fund and 80% from 
the Department of Education to oversee special education services for preschool students. 
 
Superintendent Dr. Peter Lancia stated there would be two areas of savings; 2/5ths of the Director Of Special 
Services salary and benefits and also savings from the funding from the state of Maine which was originally budgets 
at 60%, because of the number of children enrolling have 80% from the MDOE.  With those savings, Superintendent 
Dr. Peter Lancia is requesting to hire another assistant director of special services (1 year only) and access the needs 
of the special services department and Pre K enrollment next year in advance of next years’ budget. 
 
Superintendent Dr. Peter Lancia handed out spring achievement data put together by Assistant Superintendent Dr. 
O'Donnell.  Superintendent Dr. Peter Lancia thanked Dr. O'Donnell for the data and her six ( 6) years of service 
acknowledging the outstanding work that she's done helping to lead the district and helping to support curriculum as 
well as the policy committee, transportation, technology, communications, so many different roles that she's held. She 
will be the Assistant Superintendent in Scarborough Public Schools.

Superintendent Dr. Perter Lancia shared that he was bringing forth the appointment of Jeff Guerette to the position of 
Principal of Westbrook High School and Patrick Colgan as Assistant Superintendent at Westbrook High School which 
comes about from a restructuring of administration at Westbrook High School.  The new administrative team at 
Westbrook High School will be a Principal and two assistant principals. 
 
Superintendent Dr. Peter Lancia explained that Mr. Guerette applied for the position of Principal and Mr. Colgan for 
the Assistant position and after careful consideration it was decided to appoint them to their desired position.   
 
Superintendent Dr. Peter Lancia expressed confidence in Mr. Guerette and Mr. Colgan as both have helped to define 
the high community and will continue to provide strong leadership. 
 
Superintendent Dr. Peter Lancia announced a forum about technology at Westbrook High School on August 18th.  
Westbrook High School administration and leadership teams have been meeting to discuss how the ‘bell-to-bell’ 
policy of electronic devices will work. 
 
Superintendent Dr. Peter Lancia thanked Mayor David Morse and the Westbrook Education Foundation for moving 
forward the Metro pass program for students which will help students, especially within walking distance, get to school 
on time and providing them access to get to part time jobs and connect with the Greater Portland area. 
 
Chair Andrea Mancuso expressed her excitement at this opportunity for students to be able to access the Metro to get 
to school on time, jobs and medical appointments.  She explained this began with conversations through the ad hoc 
Transportation Committee and Principal Guerette and his team and the need to address attendance and students 
within the walking distance.  She thanked Mayor David Morse and the collaboration with City Council and City Hall

Memorandum 
To: Westbrook School Committee 
From: Brian Mazjanis, Assistant Superintendent of School Finance 
Date: August 4, 2026 
Subject: Request for Approval of Five-Year Lease Purchase Agreement for Special Education 
Transportation Van 
I am requesting the School Committee’s approval to enter into a five-year lease purchase 
agreement for the acquisition of a van to transport special education pre-kindergarten 
students. The total cost of the agreement will not exceed $70,000. 
The van is needed to provide safe and reliable transportation services for our youngest special 
education students and to ensure that the district can continue to meet the transportation 
requirements outlined in students’ individualized education programs (IEPs). 
The Maine Department of Education (DOE) has deemed this request reasonable and necessary 
and has approved this acquisition as a capitalized expense and has agreed to reimburse the 
district for the lease payments over the five-year term of the agreement. As a result, the cost of 
the vehicle will not have an impact on the local operating budget. We have received written 
documentation from the DOE confirming its approval of this capitalized purchase and the 
associated reimbursement. 
Recommended Motion: 
Move that the Westbrook School Committee authorize the Superintendent and Assistant 
Superintendent of School Finance to enter into a five-year lease purchase agreement, not to 
exceed $70,000, for the purchase of a van to transport special education pre-kindergarten 
students. 
Thank you for your consideration of this request.
